authoring.name: project.create
authoring.description: Initialize an empty bound directory with local, editable video source. Never overwrites an existing project.

authoring.name: project.inspect
authoring.description: Read this project's source and editing capabilities.

authoring.name: source.read
authoring.description: Read project source and its strong revision before editing.

authoring.name: source.write
authoring.description: Save source with the exact revision read; null means create-only. Uses the native Studio history.

authoring.name: element.inspect
authoring.description: Read stable scoped element ids, text, timing and editable properties.

authoring.name: element.edit
authoring.description: Apply typed SDK operations to explicit targets. Read source revision first; dryRun never writes.

authoring.name: animation.edit
authoring.description: Edit GSAP tween/keyframes using the native SDK; unsupported animation patterns return an error.

authoring.name: timeline.read
authoring.description: Read the native project timeline with source file references and bounded clip rows.

authoring.name: timeline.apply
authoring.description: Apply native timeline edits atomically. Supply all sourceVersions from timeline.read; dryRun never writes.

authoring.name: history.undo
authoring.description: Undo one recorded operation, preserving later conflicting edits.

authoring.name: asset.import
authoring.description: Copy a workspace-local media/font file into project assets without overwriting. Handles large files without base64.

authoring.name: catalog.search
authoring.description: Search the registry pinned into this plugin. Results are complete or paginated, never fetched from a floating registry.

authoring.name: catalog.add
authoring.description: Install editable source for a pinned registry item and its dependencies without overwriting. Items needing external/binary assets return TEMPLATE_ASSET_REQUIRED.

authoring.name: frame.capture
authoring.description: Render saved source at up to eight exact times. Read each returned PNG with the provided read_file arguments to actually see it.

authoring.name: project.check
authoring.description: Run native lint and browser audits on a frozen project revision. Read checksPassed and the full report, not just invocation success.

authoring.name: render
authoring.description: Render a revision-frozen MP4/WebM. Use plugin_call async:true for progress, and plugin_cancel to stop the worker.

studio.name: studio_look
studio.title: Look at the composition
studio.description: Read HyperFrames Studio's live state in one call: the open project and composition, the playhead and duration, what the human currently has selected (including what that element will and will not accept), and the live nested scene in DOM preorder. Each scene element includes source ownership, hierarchy, and optional timeline timing. `clips` lists every timeline clip, audio included: kind, start, duration, track, volume, volume/effect automation points, playback rate, audio group and role. Pass a handle back to any tool that edits an element. Returns an object with `ok: true`, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and often a `hint`. `history.undoLabel` is worth checkpointing before a batch: if it later names something you did not do, a human pressed undo and your earlier edits are gone.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against element label, tag, and handle.

limit.description: Cap the returned elements and clips (default and max 200 each). elementCount and clipCount always report the full match count.

studio.name: studio_select
studio.title: Select an element
studio.description: Select an element in HyperFrames Studio, exactly as clicking it would: the human sees the same selection box and inspector. Call this before the first write to a target so the human sees the agent's intent. Takes a handle from studio_look. Selection is visual context for the human; element writes take their own explicit handle and do not require this tool first. Returns `ok: true` with the resulting selection, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and a `hint`.

studio.name: studio_seek
studio.title: Move the playhead
studio.description: Move the playhead to a time in seconds. Pauses playback. Out-of-range times are clamped by the player, so check the returned `playhead` for where it actually landed rather than assuming it matched your request. Returns `ok: true`, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and a `hint`.

studio.name: studio_frame
studio.title: See the composition
studio.description: Render the composition to a PNG at a given time and return its URL, so you can SEE the result instead of inferring it from source. Use this to judge a change: edit, capture the instant it affects, look, adjust. The frame is rendered from the file on disk, not the live preview. A capture taken immediately after an edit can therefore predate that edit, because the render cache is cleared by a file watcher. The tool waits briefly to cover that; raise `settleMs` if a frame still looks stale, rather than concluding the edit failed. Returns `ok: true` with `url` and the `time` actually captured, or `ok: false`.

time.description: Seconds. Omit to capture wherever the playhead already is.

settleMs.description: Wait this long before capturing so a just-made edit is included. Default 150.

studio.name: studio_inspect
studio.title: Inspect one element
studio.description: Everything about one element: its resolved styles, its text fields, its box, its GSAP animations, and crucially what it will and will not accept. Read this BEFORE editing. `can` tells you which edits are possible and `can.reasonIfDisabled` says why one is not, so you can avoid a write that would be refused. Animations are only readable for the CURRENT selection; `animationEditingBlocked` says when and why animation editing is unavailable. Returns `ok: true`, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and a `hint`.

handle.description: An element handle from studio_look. Omit to inspect the current selection.

studio.name: studio_set_text
studio.title: Set an element's text
studio.description: Set one element's text using its source-safe handle from studio_look. This is the edit a synthetic double-click cannot reach, because Studio's canvas takes pointer capture and recognises the double press itself. Returns `ok: true` with the resulting text and whether it changed, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and usually a `hint` naming what to do instead. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

field.description: Which text field to write, from studio_inspect. Omit for the element's own text.

studio.name: studio_set_style
studio.title: Set an element's styles
studio.description: Set inline styles on one element using its source-safe handle from studio_look. Each property is a separate commit, so N properties produce N undo entries. Position and size properties (left, top, width, height) are refused here on purpose; they belong to the transform tools. Returns `ok: true` with `applied` and `rejected` maps, so a partial success is visible as a partial success rather than reported as a whole one. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

styles.description: CSS property to value, for example {"color": "red", "font-size": "48px"}.

studio.name: studio_transform
studio.title: Move, resize or rotate
studio.description: Move, resize or rotate one element using its source-safe handle from studio_look. Give x with y, and width with height. The result's `box` is READ BACK after the write, not echoed from your request, and `applied` lists what actually took effect. Check it. Move and rotate are written as GSAP code, so in a composition with no GSAP timeline they do nothing; that shows up in `unchanged` rather than as a false success. Rotation is reported as dispatched rather than verified, because the CSS `rotate` property does not appear in the element's computed transform. Returns `ok: true`, or `ok: false` with `kind`, `reason` and a `hint`. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

x.description: New x offset in pixels. Must be paired with y.

y.description: New y offset in pixels. Must be paired with x.

width.description: New width. Must be paired with height.

height.description: New height. Must be paired with width.

studio.name: studio_add_animation
studio.title: Add an animation
studio.description: Add a GSAP animation to one element using its source-safe handle from studio_look. It is inserted AT THE PLAYHEAD, which this tool does not control: call studio_seek first to choose when it starts. The result reports where the playhead actually was. Success means persistence and live-preview synchronization have finished. Inspect afterward when exact authored values matter. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

studio.name: studio_update_animation
studio.title: Change an animation
studio.description: Change an existing animation's duration, ease or position. It waits for persistence and live-preview synchronization before reporting success. Get current ids from studio_inspect. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

ease.description: A GSAP ease, for example power2.out.

studio.name: studio_add_keyframe
studio.title: Add a keyframe
studio.description: Add a keyframe to an existing animation at a percentage through it. All the properties land in one commit, so they are one undo entry. Reports what was dispatched, not what landed: the keyframe actor does not report back. Call studio_inspect to see the result. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.

properties.description: GSAP property to value, for example {"y": -50, "opacity": 0}.

studio.name: studio_delete_animation
studio.title: Remove an animation
studio.description: Remove an animation from the element named by handle. Undo reverses it. Success means persistence and live-preview synchronization have finished. Inspect afterward when exact authored values matter. Read `stage` as the proof level: refused, dispatched, saved, verified, or failed. `changed` is separate, and evidence explains what was actually proven.

handle.description: A source-safe element handle from studio_look.
